newsitem.title: UK: Hysterectomy not always necessary, experts say.
newsitem.headline: Hysterectomy not always necessary, experts say.

text.p: Hysterectomy is not always necessary for women who have excess bleeding during menstrual periods, British doctors reported on Friday.
They said women with menorrhagia -- excessive menstrual bleeding -- were just as well served by less invasive surgery.
Adam Magos and colleagues at London's Royal Free Hospital tested 172 women with menorraghia.
Half got the standard hysterectomy, or removal of the uterus. The rest were treated with electrosurgery or laser to remove some of the surface of the uterus, a procedure known as TCRE.
Time spent being operated on, blood loss and time to recovery are all lower with TCRE. In addition, there has been much criticism of surgeons accused of unnecessarily removing women's uteruses.

They found 85 percent of those who got TCRE were satisfied and required no further treatment, while 96 percent of those who had a hysterectomy were. There were no differences in follow-up medical needs.
"TCRE is an acceptable alternative to hysterectomy in the treatment of menorraghia for many women with no other serious disorders," they wrote in a report in the Lancet medical journal.
